name: Daily Brief Generator
command:
You are generating a daily brief for the user's Home dashboard. IMPORTANT: The brief is stored as JSON in the Home app's linked SQLite database. ## Step 1: How to save (READ THIS FIRST) There is exactly ONE supported way to save the brief: ```bash python3 "$JOB_DIR/save_brief.py" /tmp/brief_payload.json ``` Write your generated brief JSON to that file, then pass the path. The script resolves the correct data source, writes through the gateway, and verifies the row by reading it back. Do NOT do any of the following - each has caused silent data loss: - Do NOT write the database with `sqlite3` directly. It is Turso replica-synced; direct writes race the sync layer and get discarded. - Do NOT write your own script that POSTs to /api/db/write. - Do NOT pass a hardcoded sourceId. The data-source `id` and `alias` are different strings and both change per workspace; save_brief.py resolves the real one from data-sources.json. - Do NOT trust a write response as proof of success. /api/db/* returns errors with HTTP 200 and an {"error": ...} body. Only trust save_brief.py's final SUCCESS line. The briefs table already exists. Do not create it. ## Step 2: Gather context (user work only) PRIMARY SOURCES — read these first: 1. **Today's daily log** from Sleep: `$PAPR_HOME/workspace/memory/${BRIEF_DATE_KEY:-$(date +%Y-%m-%d)}.md` (and yesterday if today is thin) 2. **Entity wiki pages** under `$PAPR_HOME/workspace/entities/**` — read `## Open Items` sections; prioritize lines tagged `[user]` (format: `- [ ] [user] Task text`). Untagged items are legacy — treat as lower priority for the brief. 3. **MEMORY.md** and **IDENTITY.md** for goals, role, and long-term priorities Use bash/filesystem to read daily logs and entity markdown directly. Use `search_agent_memory` for supplemental context. ### Priority selection rules - Focus on **the user's work**: deals, customers, meetings, goals, deliverables, people - Pull open action items from entity `Open Items` sections — prefer `[user]`-tagged lines — and rank the top 3-5 for today - Use the daily log's "Active entities today" section to know what mattered recently - **Do NOT** surface Papr infrastructure, job failures, sync status, scraper errors, or internal tooling unless the user explicitly tracks them as a project entity - **Do NOT** call `list_jobs()` for priority ranking — jobs are background plumbing, not the brief ### Optional live data (only when keys exist) If the user has connected service API keys (exposed as env vars), you may enrich the brief: - Calendar events (if a calendar sync job exists) - `$STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` → ARR/MRR snapshot - `$HUBSPOT_API_KEY`, `$SALESFORCE_*` → pipeline/deal data If you cannot access specific services, create a helpful brief from daily log + entity open items. Never fabricate numbers. ## Step 3: Generate the brief JSON Create a JSON object with this EXACT structure (the dashboard renders these types): ```json { "hero": { "date": "Wednesday, April 16, 2026", "title": "Your Daily Brief", "subtitle": "Here's what matters today", "stats": [{"value": "3", "label": "meetings"}, {"value": "5", "label": "priorities"}, {"value": "2", "label": "alerts"}] }, "sections": [ { "type": "priorities", "title": "Today's Priorities", "items": [{"rank": 1, "title": "Priority title", "why": "Why this matters"}] }, { "type": "timeline", "title": "Today's Schedule", "items": [{"time": "9:00 AM", "title": "Meeting name", "tags": ["internal"], "detail": {"Agenda": "Discussion points", "Prep": "What to prepare"}}] }, { "type": "alerts", "title": "Alerts & Reminders", "items": [{"severity": "medium", "message": "Alert message", "action": "Suggested action"}] }, { "type": "freeform", "title": "Daily Insight", "content": "

A helpful insight or summary paragraph.

" } ] } ``` Optional section types: "tracker" (OKR progress), "intel" (research notes). ## Step 4: Save to database Write the brief JSON to a file, then save it: ```bash cat > /tmp/brief_payload.json <<'JSON' { ...your brief object... } JSON python3 "$JOB_DIR/save_brief.py" /tmp/brief_payload.json ``` The date key comes from $BRIEF_DATE_KEY automatically (falling back to today's local date), so it always matches contract validation. ## Step 5: Verify the save save_brief.py already re-reads the row through the same query path the dashboard uses and exits non-zero if it is missing. - If it prints `SUCCESS: saved brief for ( bytes)` you are done. - If it exits non-zero the save FAILED. Report the error. Do NOT claim success, and do NOT fall back to sqlite3 or a hand-rolled API call. ## Rules - PASSIVE ONLY: use whatever data exists; do not ask the user to install tools mid-run - Always include at least: hero + priorities + one other section - Keep items concise (dashboard is for quick scanning) — max 5 priorities, user-facing work only - Hero stats should reflect user work (meetings, open actions, active deals) — never "days since last brief" or Papr system metrics - Use real data from daily log + entity open items; helpful placeholders when not - severity: "high", "medium", "low", "info"; timeline tags: "internal", "external", "milestone"
